title: Communications Support
organization_description: The Mission Motor aims to accelerate the impact of the animal and vegan advocacy community through the use of ample evidence regarding which interventions are impactful and why. We offer training and support on Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning, so organizations can make the highest achievable impact, when data gathered through MEL helps them to continuously improve processes and interventions. .
description: Role Purposes Edit and share Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) knowledge, tools, approaches, and insights to: Improve the farmed animal movement’s understanding of the benefits and limitations of MEL. Contribute to suitable MEL practices in the animal movement. Provide MEL practitioners with easy access to best-practice, robust MEL tools. Raise TMM’s profile as an expert on best-practice MEL in the farmed animal movement. Support the Executive Director in report writing for planning and fundraising. Why Does This Role Exist? TMM regularly observes that MEL in the animal movement is not yet used properly, nor to its full potential of a combination of improving interventions, accountability, and demonstrating the (in)effectiveness of interventions. Instead, MEL is frequently used for trying to demonstrate impact too early in a program’s life cycle, or the wrong kind of accountability is applied by simply ticking boxes to keep funders satisfied. TMM believes it’s important to more clearly and broadly communicate about the benefits, limitations, and importance of using suitable MEL, while making best-practice tools freely available. We also want to communicate better about our services, plans, successes, and learnings to funders and other stakeholders. To do so, the Executive Director needs assistance with general report writing and grant writing, and the creation of presentations. The Communications Officer will play a vital role in improving TMM’s external communications. Desired Outcomes of This Role Our MEL messages, templates, and other MEL resources reach the right people, after which many actively engage with the content. TMM delivers informative and engaging presentations at key gatherings. Reports and grant proposals are engaging, professional, and accurate. Key Activities Building out our current communication strategy, suitable to reach the goals stated above, including key target audiences, key communication channels, a communication plan, and timeline. Our current communication channels are our website and LinkedIn, and several targeted forums and mailing lists from others. Supporting the MEL Advisors and Executive Director to create MEL content (blogs, updates, presentations), grant proposals, reports, and the annual plan. Tasks include: Together with the Program Lead and Director, creating a communication plan that lists concrete topics, specifies the writer, and a timeline. Informing designated writers of the topics and timeline. Supporting and facilitating the writers as much as possible. Informing the Program Lead if deadlines for write-ups are not met. Providing feedback on drafts. Data visualization through, e.g., the creation of infographics. Final editing of communication materials. Publishing all TMM communication pieces on the suitable channels, including embedding tools and templates on the TMM website, and potentially a TMM newsletter. Problem solving of communication channels. Data collection on reach and progress towards our outcomes. The role does not require giving presentations or being the spokesperson for the organization. Decision-Making Authority With input from the team, and within the framework approved by the Executive Director, you set the communication strategy. Final responsibility for the lay-out and phrasing of all communication materials. Deliverables are reviewed by the Executive Director and Team Lead. Profile of the Communications Officer Ability to translate scientific “professional” language into regular, easy-to-understand language or other communication tools while maintaining the quality of the content. Accurate final editing of all content in USA English. Comfortable taking responsibility for communications output. Familiar with Effective Altruism principles. Familiar with the farmed animal movement. Good interpersonal skills, able to create buy-in and nudge. Data visualization skills and experience. Nice to have: Experience with and interest in working and experimenting with frontier AI models (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.). Experience with Squarespace and with HTML/JavaScript, or willingness to learn. Ability to use, e.g., Claude Code to create technically coding modules on the website, or strong interest in learning how to do this. Some budget is available to hire additional support or upskill in certain areas if necessary. Commitments & Norms Actively engage and collaborate with the other team members. Around 4 hours per day overlap with the UK (GMT) timezone mid-day. Some flexibility towards working times is expected in order to interact with team members in different countries. Use of TMM’s standard tools such as Slack, Airtable, and Notion. Priority Setting The following trade-offs guide the priorities of communication: Collaboration and support, even over speed. Critical reflection and learning, even over perfection. Benefit of the movement, even over benefit of TMM. Sustainable systems, even over short-term wins.

title: Research Program Lead
organization_description: Animal Welfare League is a nonprofit working with corporate companies to improve farmed-animal welfare across Africa. We secure corporate policies through research, negotiation, peaceful public actions, and strategic media.
description: The Animal Welfare League is commissioning its first substantial body of independent research: three studies across South Africa, Nigeria and Egypt on the economics of cage-free egg production, the spread of cage systems in broiler production, and the real cost of building aviary laying hen housing in African conditions. We’re looking for someone to lead this program. This is a commissioning and quality role , not one that involves writing the research itself. You will define what gets studied, select who studies it, hold them to a rigorous standard, and ensure the results meet the expectations of the institutions, regulators, and companies whose decisions they’re meant to inform. The program is deliberately open: every study we commission is published in full, whatever the outcome, under an open license, with its underlying data. You would be responsible for protecting that openness under pressure. Primary Responsibilities Program management. Run the three 2026–27 studies on time and according to budget. Maintain the schedule against the external deadlines that matter, particularly standard processes, and proactively communicate when a deadline or deliverable is at risk. Commissioning. Draft terms of reference and calls for proposals. Run open calls and invited procurements. Assemble and service evaluation panels. Negotiate and manage contracts, milestones and payments with researchers and institutions. Research quality. Interrogate proposed methods before committing money. Ensure that protocols are pre-registered where appropriate, that assumptions are published, and that comparability is maintained where several pieces of work must be read together. Catch weak analysis before it’s published, not after. Partnerships. Work with civil society partners, academic institutions and consultants across the continent, including our collaboration with Animal Law Reform South Africa. Represent AWL in technical and standards settings when possible. Use and dissemination. Turn commissioned research and policy work into submissions, policy briefs and materials that decision-makers actually read. Track where the evidence lands and what it changes. Funding. Support applications to co-fund the program, working with the Executive Director. Our current research budget is modest, and part of this role is making it go further. Required Qualifications The ability to read a quantitative analysis or an economic model and judge whether it is sound. This is the core of the role. Experience commissioning, managing or supervising research in a non-profit, academic, government or consultancy setting. A postgraduate qualification in agricultural or applied economics, animal science, public policy, statistics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Written English to publication standard. Sound judgment about evidence, including the confidence to tell a funder, a partner or your own organization that a finding does not hold. Experience developing policy positions or engaging legislative, regulatory or institutional processes. Willingness to build a body of work in an area where little exists and to start by establishing the facts rather than by arguing a position. Comfort working remotely, independently and across time zones. Preferred Candidates Experience in African agriculture or the poultry sector. Familiarity with the Three Rs framework (Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement), animal research ethics, or institutional ethics review. Knowledge in legislative drafting, model provisions or regulatory submissions. Familiarity with standards-development processes, whether national, regional or international. Experience in research procurement, contracting or grant management. A record of published or commissioned work. Familiarity with the Open Wing Alliance or the farmed animal welfare movement. Fluency in French or Arabic. What We Offer A program with real independence written into its terms, and an organization that will back you when a finding is inconvenient. Direct influence over what gets researched on farm animal welfare in Africa, at a point when very little of it exists. The chance to build AWL’s work on animals used in research from the beginning, and to shape its direction. Flexible hours and full remote working. Named credit on the programme’s published outputs.
